{"description":"Content hash → readable name → what references it, so a design that points at stored content can say what it does NOT itself carry. `missing` names content the graph references and this checkout lacks — the case someone handed the export alone hits, where a diagram that will not open becomes a named finding instead of a silent absence. `orphaned` is the reverse: bytes stored and referenced by nothing, which is how a store grows without anyone deciding to (and the reason `dec:where-content-lives` left repo growth deliberately open).

DERIVED, NEVER STORED, and that is the design rather than an optimisation. The manifest is computed from the graph plus a directory listing; a manifest kept as its own record would be a second source of truth about what the design references and would drift the first time someone updated one and not the other. Rendering it to a committed markdown file is a PROJECTION — the same relationship `dec:views-are-projections` already sets for every other view.

THE READABLE NAME IS THE FRAGMENT'S `title`, not a filename stored beside the hash. The graph already requires a title, so there is no second place for names to live and nothing to disagree with the design about what a thing is called. `referenced_by` carries the Fragment AND what it annotates or yielded, so "what is this picture for?" is answerable from the manifest without opening anything.

A LOCATOR AFTER THE HASH TRAVELS VERBATIM and is never parsed (`dec:agent-navigates-content`) — `sha256:…#L412-L440` resolves to the same blob and reports `L412-L440` untouched. A `content_ref` holding a plain PATH from before the store existed is not treated as content at all, so legacy references do not read as missing blobs.

Needed a FOURTH store function, `list` — named rather than slipped in, because `dec:content-store-implementation` argued for three. That argument was about `object_store`'s path/prefix/pagination semantics, which immutable content addressing does not need; enumerating a flat set of addresses is a different thing, and orphan detection is impossible without it. `list` skips anything whose name is not a hash, so a stranded temp file or the committed manifest is never mistaken for content.

Paired with `.gitattributes` marking the blob directory `binary` — which stops git attempting diffs it cannot produce and, the part that matters, stops line-ending conversion silently corrupting a PNG on a CRLF checkout. REALIZED; `ver:content-manifest` passing, served as `content_manifest`.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"Say what content the design depends on, in names a person can read","provenance":"authored","status":"realized","tier":"operational"}
